meta.title: Serverless Orders on AWS
meta.description: A static web app on CloudFront, a Cognito-protected API, and an SQS-buffered fulfilment worker inside a private VPC.

summary.headline: Orders are accepted in milliseconds and fulfilled asynchronously: the API only writes the order and queues the work.
points: CloudFront serves the app from S3 and forwards /api calls to API Gateway
Cognito issues the JWT; API Gateway verifies it before any Lambda runs
SQS absorbs spikes, so fulfilment never slows down checkout
Only the fulfilment Lambda reaches into the VPC, where the inventory database lives

groups.title: AWS account (eu-west-2)
groups.description: Production account. Everything here is billed per request and scales to zero.

groups.title: Serverless backend
groups.description: Managed services only: no servers to patch, concurrency limits set per function.

groups.title: Private VPC
groups.description: Private subnets across two availability zones. No internet gateway; VPC endpoints reach SQS and DynamoDB.

data.title: Web & mobile app
data.subtitle: React SPA, iOS, Android
data.description: Customers browse the catalogue and place orders.

data.title: CloudFront
data.subtitle: CDN and TLS termination
data.description: Caches the static site at the edge and forwards /api/* to API Gateway.

data.title: S3 site bucket
data.subtitle: Static assets
data.description: Versioned bucket holding the built single-page app. Only CloudFront can read it.

data.title: Cognito user pool
data.subtitle: Sign-in and JWTs
data.description: Hosted sign-in, MFA and token issuance. API Gateway trusts its JWT issuer.

data.title: API Gateway
data.subtitle: HTTP API, JWT authoriser
data.description: Validates the Cognito token, throttles per client and invokes the orders function.

data.title: Orders Lambda
data.subtitle: Accepts and records orders
data.description: Validates the basket, writes the order with a conditional put and queues fulfilment.

data.title: SQS fulfilment queue
data.subtitle: Buffer with dead-letter queue
data.description: Decouples checkout from fulfilment. Failed messages move to a DLQ after 5 attempts.

data.title: Fulfilment Lambda
data.subtitle: VPC-attached worker
data.description: Reserves stock, then marks the order as confirmed or back-ordered.

data.title: Aurora PostgreSQL
data.subtitle: Inventory, private subnets
data.description: Stock levels and reservations. Reachable only from inside the VPC.

data.title: DynamoDB orders
data.subtitle: On-demand table
data.description: Single-table design keyed by customer and order id.

scenarios.name: Place an order
scenarios.description: From sign-in to a confirmed, stock-reserved order.

steps.title: One account, two trust zones
steps.description: Everything runs in one AWS account. Managed services form the serverless backend; only the fulfilment worker and the inventory database sit in the private VPC.

steps.title: The customer signs in
steps.description: The app uses Cognito's hosted sign-in and receives a short-lived JWT.

steps.title: CloudFront serves the app and the API
steps.description: Static files come from the S3 bucket; requests under /api/* are forwarded to API Gateway.

steps.title: The order is accepted
steps.description: API Gateway verifies the JWT and invokes the Orders Lambda, which writes the order to DynamoDB and returns 202.

steps.title: Fulfilment is queued
steps.description: The same function drops a message on SQS. A spike in orders only lengthens the queue; checkout stays fast.

steps.title: Stock is reserved inside the VPC
steps.description: The fulfilment Lambda reserves stock in Aurora through RDS Proxy, then sets the order status in DynamoDB.
